purpose: Track the canonical definition status of binding research methods without silently promoting legacy implementations to approved methods.

legacy_candidate.observed_behavior: Creates transition feature signatures (including positional, gap, parity, band, modulo-3/5/7, sum, span, shape and signed-core changes), ranks similar historical transitions using exact/sign/absolute transforms, then votes on the matched transitions' B draw.
legacy_candidate.known_gap: The legacy evaluator scores the B state for a target transition; it does not, as written, establish a canonical A->B transition to following C-state method.

legacy_candidate.observed_behavior: Counts empirical co-occurrences from each source-draw number to numbers in the immediately following draw, then aggregates historical target-number counts for numbers present in the current source draw.
legacy_candidate.known_gap: This is a legacy source-number-to-next-draw-number candidate; the repository's canonical A->T semantics and constraints are not explicitly approved.

legacy_candidate.observed_behavior: Computes per-position residue-change values (B[i] % 5) - (A[i] % 5) as one transition signature among several.
legacy_candidate.known_gap: A modulo-5 transition-difference feature is not, by itself, an approved MOD5-to-target T mapping.

V19_best_stable_ABC_weight.meaning: Reported prior memory value; formula definition, exact evaluation protocol and run logs have not been independently reconstructed in this audit.

V0_3_1_crossover_weights.meaning: Reported prior memory values; weights do not define the algorithms or prove out-of-sample performance.

promotion_requirements: Record the exact mathematical/algorithmic definition for each method.
Preserve a traceable source/version and its applicable archive regime.
Do not use the current isolated target or any later draw during discovery or fitting.
Add deterministic synthetic unit tests before any real-archive execution.
Run forward walk-forward, reverse retrospective stress testing, and time-ordered cross-validation as separate labelled protocols.
Compare results with an appropriate random/null baseline and report uncertainty; do not claim proof from average hits alone.
Promote a method from OPEN_DEFINITION only after its definition is explicitly approved; do not change binding rules implicitly.
